newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares steady, no end to rally seen.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares steady, no end to rally seen.

text.p: Belgian shares held steady on Tuesday morning, holding up better than neighbouring markets and with analysts confident of further gains in the weeks ahead.

"The (market) rise has been impressive since the start of the year. But regarding low interest rates, the sharp increase in the dollar and earnings-per-share growth (prospects) for most companies the market is not really expensive," one said.
"I see further gains for blue chips," he added.
By 0905 GMT the Bel-20 .BFX leading index of shares stood 2.61 points or 0.11 percent higher at 2,342.25, extending its record run to touch a new high of 2,347.53.
Buying in non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere continued, with the stock rising a further 2.59 percent to 3,380 francs after it gained 2.7 percent the previous session.
One dealer pointed to news on Monday that Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said it had accepted UM's offer to buy 56 percent of the MDK copper smelter there as a reason for interest in the stock.

Kredietbank stood 0.31 percent lower at 16.025 francs, giving up some of Monday's 5.2 percent gain which followed renewed speculation about possible strategic alliances with Belgium's CERA Bank or Dutch Rabobank.
Generale Bank said in its daily research note it had downgraded the stock to 'hold' from 'buy', considering that good fundamentals were now fully discounted in the share price.
